edges.effect_quant: In the 23,637-person Walter Reed cohort, adjusted subhazard ratios for major adverse cardiovascular events were 1.4, 2.0, and 2.8 for CAC scores of 1-100, 101-400, and over 400 versus zero. In MESA, each doubling of CAC was associated with a 14% increase in 10-year ASCVD risk and CAC above 300 corresponded to 10-year event rates of roughly 13% to 26% across demographic groups.
edges.population: asymptomatic or primary-prevention adults undergoing coronary artery calcium scoring
edges.mechanism: High coronary artery calcium is a cumulative plaque-burden signal rather than a transient lab abnormality. It integrates the long-run effect of lipoprotein exposure, blood pressure, glycemic stress, and vascular inflammation, so a strong link to 10-year major cardiovascular events is biologically expected.
edges.summary: This is one of the most practically useful risk-stratification edges in the corpus. Once CAC becomes clearly elevated, 10-year major cardiovascular event risk rises in a graded way across multiple cohorts, and the main discussion shifts from whether risk is elevated to how aggressively prevention should be intensified.
edges.caveats: Coronary calcium is not identical to unstable plaque, so it predicts long-run event burden better than immediate plaque rupture risk. Absolute risk also changes with age, renal function, diabetes burden, and background preventive therapy, so CAC should be read as a strong modifier of baseline risk rather than as a standalone diagnosis.

evidence.notes: Coronary Artery Calcium and Long-Term Risk of Death, Myocardial Infarction, and Stroke: The Walter Reed Cohort Study.

new_entities.name: High coronary artery calcium score
new_entities.description: A coronary artery calcium score high enough to indicate substantial calcified atherosclerotic plaque burden on cardiac CT.

new_entities.name: 10-year major adverse cardiovascular events
new_entities.description: Composite risk of major adverse cardiovascular events over roughly 10 years, typically including myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, and related hard atherosclerotic outcomes.
